correctness.rationale: Friedman–Hoşten–Rosana Theorem 3.3 establishes the repeated-root set equality in the stated range of k. Over C, a repeated eigenvalue of a symmetric matrix has an isotropic eigenline either because its eigenspace has dimension at least two or because a Jordan predecessor u of an eigenvector v gives v^Tv=v^T(Q-lambda I)u=0. Conversely a simple root with isotropic eigenvector would give a Jordan predecessor, since the image is v-perp. Assigning a symmetric form any row and matching column in a basis beginning with v proves surjectivity of Q->Qv mod Cv. The incidence is a smooth rational kernel bundle of rank N-n+1 and dimension N-1 over the smooth irreducible quadric; the projection is proper. The discriminant is a nonempty hypersurface by the nonzero characteristic discriminant polynomial. The dense open one-double-root stratum can be defined by degree one of gcd(p,p') (a Sylvester rank condition), and defectivity on that stratum by cyclicity of Q (linear independence of I,Q,...,Q^(n-1)). The given square-zero block plus distinct simple roots lies in this open set, and there is precisely one isotropic eigenline there, proving birationality in characteristic zero. The frozen perturbation has quadratic discriminant eps^2+4i*eps and all cross-resultants nonzero at eps=0, so the irreducible support has multiplicity one. Scaling gives exact degree. The n=2 factorization is correct. The frozen finite checker was inspected, not executed; these conclusions follow analytically.

evidence: Theorem 1.7 and Sec. 1.2.A of Tevelev give conormal reflexivity and the bundle of projective tangent hyperplanes for every smooth irreducible projective X over C. When the dual is a hypersurface, its smooth hyperplane point has one tangent projective hyperplane in the dual ambient space; reflexivity identifies that with the unique contact point and gives the birational conormal projection.

Krishna computes the general determinant-discriminant Cartier class d(d-1)c1(S*) for pencils of quadrics; pencils containing I form a Plücker-linear projective subspace and the restriction has the same class. This class alone would not prove the restricted equation reduced.
Domokos's full-matrix and real-symmetric invariant results are polynomial-context comparisons, not the conormal coverage.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The projective-dual theorem applies to this smooth rational embedded quadric with a nonempty hypersurface dual. Replacing projective tangent functionals by their full vector spaces gives exactly the stated rank-(N-n+1) bundle and affine resolution. The degree can also be computed on that same projective bundle, without inferring reducedness from restriction of a class.

evidence: ED Theorem 3.3 supplies the repeated-root set equality for every k in scope; the classical pencil criterion identifies that set with the tangent hyperplanes to X. In the conormal model E is the kernel of the trivial Sym_n bundle onto L* tensor (V/L) on the quadric, where L is the tautological line.

For the reduced dual, P(E) is projectively birational. Integrating the pulled-back hyperplane class gives the degree as the integral over the quadric of s_(n-2)(E). Since s(E)=c(L* tensor (V/L))=(1+h)^n with h=c1(L*), the integral is 2*binom(n,n-2)=n(n-1). Thus the same degree is an immediate projective-bundle calculation and not merely the degree of a possibly nonreduced equation.
The complexification of the real repeated-eigenvalue locus in Breiding–Kozhasov–Lerario is not the characteristic-discriminant hypersurface used in this implication.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Known results give the identification, incidence, and birationality under identical hypotheses; a standard degree calculation then recovers the reduced hypersurface degree. The affine image is irreducible since the quadric and its vector bundle are, and rational by birationality. The elementary n=2 factorization supplies no separate new claim.

evidence: For X={ [vv^T] : v^Tv=0 } in P(Sym_n), differentiating vv^T along w in v-perp gives pairing with Q equal to 2w^TQv. Hence the functional defines a tangent hyperplane exactly when Qv lies in Cv. This identifies the projectivized frozen incidence with the conormal incidence, including functionals of the ambient space vanishing on the whole linear span.

For Q not proportional to I the tangent condition means that the intersection of v^Tv=0 and v^TQv=0 is singular. The regular-pencil criterion equates this with a repeated root of det(tI-Q). Proportional matrices also satisfy the claim (all isotropic lines in their fiber).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The classical criterion and conormal construction cover exactly the same equations and incidence points, not just nearby real loci, a similar-sounding spectral stratum, or an invariant with the same numerical degree.

originality.rationale: The apparent additional geometry is covered by the classical regular-pencil criterion combined with projective conormal reflexivity. This is statement-level implication, not an inference from a search miss. On the quadratic Veronese image X of the isotropic quadric, the conormal condition for a matrix functional Q is exactly Qv in Cv; the repeated-det-root locus is precisely the dual by the two-quadric regularity criterion. The claimed affine bundle and its projection are the affine-lifted conormal resolution of that dual, not just analogous to it. The same bundle gives the reduced degree by the standard projective bundle formula. The inspected ED paper does not itself state the resolution, and no exact duplicate Resultary record was identified. Neither fact negates broader coverage.
